title: Your First Salary Follows You Forever — $347K Cost
hook: You accepted a low first offer to 'get your foot in the door' — and that one number quietly follows every paycheck you'll ever earn.
angle: Salary anchoring is a compound wealth-killer: raises are percentage-based, employers anchor new offers on your current pay, and $5K underearned at 22 cascades into $347K lost by 60. Most workers have no idea their first salary is their most consequential financial decision.
audience: Workers 22–40 who took their first offer or are underpaid relative to market — especially those who've never job-hopped
key_numbers: $5K below-market first salary cascades to $347K lost over a 30-year career
72% of employers anchor their opening offer to your current or past salary
Job-hoppers earn 50% more lifetime than employees who stay loyal
Every $1K underearned at 22 costs roughly $60K by retirement
Only 37% of people negotiate their first salary offer
